name: GE Vernova
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: GE Vernova controls the scarcest resources in the AI power buildout — heavy-duty gas turbine slots and North American transformer capacity — with 116 GW of gas capacity committed (53 GW equipment backlog plus 63 GW of deposit-backed slot reservations) as of Q2 2026, reservations now selling against 2031 delivery, and data-center electrification orders that quintupled inside 18 months ($2.4B in Q1 2026 alone, more than all of 2025). BACKGROUND: Spun from General Electric April 2024; ~85,000 employees; installed base of ~7,000 gas turbines and equipment behind ~25% of world electricity. Three segments — Power (gas/hydro/nuclear/steam), Wind (loss-making), Electrification (grid equipment, now including 100%-owned transformer maker Prolec GE, acquired for $5.275B February 2026). FY2025 revenue $38.1B; total backlog $176B at Q2 2026. Named NVIDIA 800 VDC partner with three AI-factory reference designs (grid-connected, islanded, bridging).
ecosystemRole: We assess GE Vernova as the single best lens on the report's time-to-power question: whoever holds turbine slots and transformer capacity sets the energization date for every gigawatt-class campus, and GEV holds more of both than anyone in the Americas. Basis: turbine reservations sold out through ~2030 with ~$3,000/kW implied combined-cycle pricing (roughly triple three years ago), transformer lead times industry-wide at 2.5-4 years with Prolec GE now wholly owned, and hyperscalers routing around the grid queue via GEV hardware — Chevron's 4 GW 'power foundries' (seven 7HA turbines), Crusoe's LM2500XPRESS aeroderivative fleets, and Oracle Abilene's on-site turbines. For BESS vendors, GEV is both channel and competitor: its aeroderivative-plus-BESS bridging configurations and FLEXRESERVOIR storage line compete for the same behind-the-fence scope.

productsAndServices.name: Heavy-duty gas turbines (7HA/9HA family)
productsAndServices.description: The 7HA flagship line: 7HA.01 (290 MW), 7HA.02 (384 MW), 7HA.03 (430 MW simple-cycle), 42.0-43.3% simple-cycle net efficiency and 63-64% combined-cycle; ramp rates to 75 MW/min, ~10-minute hot starts, up to 50% hydrogen-capable. Sold via orders plus paid slot-reservation agreements (~20% cash down) that convert to orders — Q2 2026 alone converted 10 GW of reservations.
productsAndServices.positioning: One of three OEMs (with Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi Power) supplying two-thirds of turbines for gas plants under construction globally; largest single share of heavy-duty (>14.5% per GMInsights). Slot pricing 10-20 points above the existing backlog is the clearest scarcity-rent evidence in the sector.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct equipment sales + long-term service agreements; EPC-agnostic.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Output ramps from ~20 GW/yr (Q3 2026 run-rate) to 24 GW in 2028, actions toward 30 GW by 2030; expected 'largely sold out of 2030 deliveries by end of 2026.'

productsAndServices.name: Aeroderivative turbines & bridging power (LM2500/LM6000/TM2500)
productsAndServices.description: Fast-deploy prime and bridge power for data centers: LM6000 with 5-minute starts (1,300+ units fielded), LM2500XPRESS packaged units (>99.8% availability, powering Crusoe AI data centers), TM2500 mobile units installed in 11 days. Four offered data-center configurations including onsite prime power and grid-connected hybrid with battery.
productsAndServices.positioning: The 'two weeks to power generation' pitch versus multi-year interconnection queues — competing against Bloom fuel cells, Caterpillar/Cummins gensets, and Solaris mobile turbines for the bridge-power wedge.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through power-as-a-service developers (Crusoe, VoltaGrid-class operators).
targetSegments: AI data centers needing bridge/prime power
productsAndServices.roadmap: Belfort, France line adds +2 GW of ~90 MW 7E-class industrial turbines aimed squarely at bridge-power demand, no new capex.

productsAndServices.name: Electrification — transformers, switchgear, HVDC (incl. Prolec GE)
productsAndServices.description: Power Transmission: power/distribution transformers (Prolec GE: ~10,000 employees, seven Americas plants, five in the US), gas- and air-insulated switchgear 50-800 kV, HV breakers. Grid Systems Integration: HVDC (six consecutive 2 GW bipole contracts with TenneT), AC substations, and direct data-center complex solutions. Grid stability: STATCOMs, synchronous condensers, SVCs.
productsAndServices.positioning: Hitachi Energy leads global transformers with Siemens Energy, Eaton, GEV, Toshiba in the top tier — but Prolec makes GEV the most North America-weighted. Wood Mackenzie has power-transformer lead times at ~2.5 years and prices predicted to rise through 2030; GEV owns the bottleneck's American toll booth.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility and hyperscaler direct contracts; Q4 2025 was the segment's largest-ever quarter of orders directly from hyperscalers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Data-center Electrification orders: ~$0.7B (2024) → >$2B (2025) → >$5B in 1H 2026 alone. ~$1B Prolec capex 2026-28; Charleroi PA ($138M) and Italy bushings expansions underway.

productsAndServices.name: Solid-state transformers & NVIDIA 800 VDC reference designs
productsAndServices.description: Three jointly-developed AI-factory reference designs with NVIDIA (grid-connected, islanded, bridging power) centered on 800 VDC — 13.8 kV AC converted to 800 VDC at the perimeter via solid-state transformers and industrial rectifiers, with digital twins in NVIDIA's Omniverse DSX Blueprint. An R&D cost-share with a hyperscaler carries a commitment to buy 1,000 SSTs from 2027 if spec is met.
productsAndServices.positioning: The SST is the architectural leap that could collapse the AC distribution chain — GEV is the only grid-equipment incumbent with a disclosed hyperscaler SST purchase commitment attached to a development milestone.
productsAndServices.roadmap: SST cited as 12-24 months from commercialization, 24-36 from industrialization (December 2025 investor update).

productsAndServices.name: BESS & solar (FLEXRESERVOIR, RESTORE, FLEXINVERTER)
productsAndServices.description: FLEXRESERVOIR containerized grid-scale BESS (batteries + power electronics + controls); RESTORE DC Block modular 5 MWh units spanning 2-8 hour durations; FLEXINVERTER utility-scale PCS platform; FLEXIQ EMS. Term sheet with Our Next Energy (ONE) for US-made LFP cells.
productsAndServices.positioning: A second-tier BESS integrator by shipment share, but sold with generation and grid scope the pure-plays lack — most relevant to this file as the storage arm of GEV's islanded/bridging AI-factory designs.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility and project contracts, generation-coupled hybrids.
productsAndServices.roadmap: US LFP supply (ONE) addresses domestic-content procurement; storage sits inside the Power Conversion & Storage unit (~$5B backlog end-2025).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess GEV holds genuine multi-year pricing power in gas turbines, and that it is scarcity rent rather than durable moat. Basis: reservations selling for 2031 delivery at ~$3,000/kW implied combined-cycle pricing (~3x in three years), 20%-cash-down slot agreements, and capacity 'largely sold out of 2030' — while Siemens Energy nearly doubled unit sales year-over-year and Mitsubishi calls its own +30% capacity add 'not enough.' Competitor supply lands in the same 2028-2030 windows GEV is now selling.

(High confidence) We assess the transformer bottleneck is the more defensible franchise. Basis: industry lead times of 2.5-4 years with shortage modeled to persist toward 2030 (Wood Mackenzie), Prolec GE's five US plants now wholly owned, and data-center electrification orders quintupling in 18 months — equipment margin in backlog rose 6 points in 2025.

(Moderate confidence) We assess backlog-to-revenue conversion is the central risk the headline numbers hide. Basis: $176B backlog and 116 GW committed sit upstream of interconnection queues, gas-supply infrastructure, and possible data-center demand revisions; slot deposits (~20%) mitigate but do not eliminate slippage or cancellation, and adjusted EPS missed in two of the last four reported periods even as orders broke records.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the SST program is the highest-leverage optionality in the file's grid segment. Basis: a hyperscaler-funded development deal with a 1,000-unit purchase commitment from 2027 — if the spec lands, GEV leapfrogs the AC-switchboard incumbents into the 800 VDC perimeter; if it slips, the referenced ~$13B SST market forms around Heron Power-class challengers instead.

(Low confidence) We assess wind will keep subtracting roughly $400M of EBITDA annually through 2026-27 with limited strategic exit options. Basis: losses overshot guidance in 2025 (~$600M vs ~$400M), the December 2025 federal stop-work order forced further offshore contract-loss accruals, and management's language ('focusing on what we can control') signals containment, not resolution.
